<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1316
Claimant:
Heather King
Adjuster:
Jerry Hanson
2024-06-03
First notice of loss came in from the claimant, who reported being rear-ended while stopped at a signal. The claimant
is not rerpesented by an attorney and has asked to handle the file directly.
2024-07-12
Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of the incident. Nothing in the
policy history suggests the damage predates the coverage start.
2024-07-27
Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. Two statements from people
nearby were requested, but no independent witnesses have been identified so far.
2024-08-11
Scheduled a physical inspection of the claimant's vehicle. The rear bumper damage and crushed panel are consistent
with the impact described in the first notice.
2024-08-26
Reviewed the scene photos submitted by the claimant. They confirm several details of the account, though a few
older scratches on the rear panel may predate this crash and will need to be separated out in the estimate.
2024-09-04
Claimant reported a knee injruy and provided initial medical paperwork. It is not yet clear whether the injury came
from this collision, and causation remains open pending records.
2024-10-07
Claimant called to add a few small detalis about the seating position and the moment of impact. The core account is
unchanged from the first notice. No prior injury to the same knee has been reported or found in the records requested
so far.
2024-12-16
Treatment records show a usual course of care that tapered off as the claimant improved. Requested the complete
chart and prior-provider history to confirm the timeline and any gaps.
2024-12-26
File remains open. Next steps are to finish the repair estimate with the older scratches excluded and to complete the
causation review of the knee injury before any settlement discussion.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
